Header: Commelina benghalensis . Inteja (Kinyarwanda); Comméline du Bengale (French); Bengal dayflower (English)

Prevention: Proper land preparation (deep tillage) to ensure removal of the entire plant including roots and fragments to avoid seed dispersal
Avoid the use of mulching materials that contain fragments of commelina
Intercrop banana with crops such as bush beans to cover the soil and suppress the weed
Monitoring: Look for creeping broadleaved herb with stems trailing along the ground, or ascending; with dark green leaves, and small blue petals
Regular (once per week) field assessment for initial infestations to guide timely control
Take control action (hand weeding) when the weed density is estimated at 30% ground cover
Direct Control: Uprooting/pulling out the weed, taking care to remove all parts as fragments can sprout
Remove by hand hoeing, taking care to remove all parts as fragments can sprout
Shake off soil, spread them out to allow them to dry with time
In case of heavy infestations in big and/or commercial plantations, apply 2, 4-Dichloro-phenoxyacetic acid (2, 4-D).
Apply 720g/L, when weeds are 3 weeks old and crop is also at least 3 weeks old to avoid herbicide side effects on the main crop and pay attention to adjacent field crops
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage

Do not spray 2,4-D if rain seems likely within 6hours or if strong winds prevail; Do not apply 2,4-D if crop or weed are stressed due to dry or excessively moist conditions; r.e.i. 2 days; p.h.i.: 40 days

Diuron on very light sandy or gravelly soils as crop damage may occur; Do not apply more than once per calendar year; Apply it if greater than 50mm rain is expected within 3 days of application; restricted re- entry interval r.e.i. ½ day; pre-harvest interval p.h.i.: 20 days
